title: Boeing FY2022 10-K — Note 21 – Legal Proceedings, opening scope and materiality standard (p.108)
key_points: Note 21 covers legal proceedings, claims and investigations related to products, contracts, employment and other matters.
Boeing is also subject to various U.S. government inquiries and investigations from which civil, criminal or administrative proceedings could result or have resulted in the past.
Such government proceedings could involve claims for fines, penalties, compensatory and treble damages, restitution and/or forfeitures.
Under government regulations a company or its divisions can be suspended or debarred from government contracts, or lose export privileges, based on investigation results.
Boeing states that, except as described in the note, it believes outcomes will not have a material effect on financial position, results of operations or cash flows.
Where a loss in excess of recorded amounts is reasonably possible, Boeing discloses either the amount/range or the reasons no estimate can be made.
raw_excerpt:
Note 21 – Legal Proceedings
Various legal proceedings, claims and investigations related to products, contracts, employment and other matters are pending against us. In addition, we are subject to various U.S. government inquiries and investigations from which civil, criminal or administrative proceedings could result or have resulted in the past. Such proceedings involve or could involve claims by the government for fines, penalties, compensatory and treble damages, restitution and/or forfeitures. Under government regulations, a company, or one or more of its operating divisions or subdivisions, can also be suspended or debarred from government contracts, or lose its export privileges, based on the results of investigations. Except as described below, we believe, based upon current information, that the outcome of any such legal proceeding, claim, or government dispute and investigation will not have a material effect on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K — Note 21: Embraer joint-venture termination dispute in arbitration
key_points: In 2019 Boeing entered agreements with Embraer S.A. to establish joint ventures including Embraer's commercial aircraft and services operations, with Boeing expected to acquire an 80 percent ownership stake for $4,200 (million).
In 2020 Boeing exercised its contractual right to terminate the agreements based on Embraer's failure to meet certain required closing conditions.
Embraer disputes Boeing's right to terminate, and the dispute is currently in arbitration.
Boeing cannot reasonably estimate a range of loss, if any, from the arbitration, which it expected to be completed in late 2023 or early 2024.

title: BOEING_2022_10K — 787 项目：交付暂停、FAA 恢复交付授权与异常生产成本
key_points: 787 交付于 2021 年 5 月暂停，原因是生产质量问题（包括供应链中的问题）；此前 2021 年 3 月至 5 月间已交付 14 架。
2022 年 7 月 28 日获得 FAA 恢复交付授权，2022 年 8 月恢复交付；2022 年全年交付 31 架。
2022 年末与 2021 年末分别约有 100 架和 110 架 787 在库存中；2022 年末库存中的大部分飞机预计在 2024 年底前交付。
2022 年第四季度将 787 异常生产成本总额估计上调至 28 亿美元，其中大部分将在 2023 年底前发生；2021 年末预期累计约 20 亿美元。
2022 年 787 异常生产成本计入 12.40 亿美元。
公司仍在低速率生产，预计 2023 年逐步恢复至每月 5 架。
raw_excerpt: We received FAA authorization to resume delivery on July 28, 2022 and deliveries resumed in August. During 2022, we delivered 31 aircraft to customers. ... we adjusted the total estimate of abnormal production costs up to $2.8 billion with most being incurred by the end of 2023.

title: BOEING_2022_10K — 737 项目：生产速率、FAA 型号认证与 ACSAA 第 116 条修订
key_points: 2022 年将 737 生产速率提升至每月 31 架，并计划依据市场需求与供应链能力进一步逐步提产。
737-7 与 737-10 正在接受 FAA 型号认证；公司预计 737-7 于 2023 年取证并交付，737-10 于 2023 年开始 FAA 认证试飞、2024 年首交付。
《2023 年综合拨款法》修订了 ACSAA 第 116 条，使 2020 年 12 月 27 日前提交的原始或修订型号认证申请（含 737-7 与 737-10）不再受第 116 条机组告警规格约束。
自 FAA 颁发 737-10 型号合格证满一年起，任何新的 737 MAX 飞机须包含特定安全增强才能获得原始适航认证；公司已为相关改装成本计提，且预计不重大。
raw_excerpt: We increased the production rate to 31 per month in 2022 ...
